findings.issue: Trust boundary: the category rule and the caption rule are checked only in the browser, in validateVersion via schemaFor('scenes') -> scenesSchema. The publish path is CollectionForm -> PublishBar -> publishDocument (admin-publish.ts:89-93) -> validateVersion (46-82) -> rpc('publish_version'). The SQL side, public.publish_version (supabase/migrations/20260927090000_static_site_and_functions.sql:51-65) -> content_assert_publisher -> content_go_live (20260925120000_content_versions_and_publishing.sql:133), never looks at the data. No edge function is involved, and there is no trigger on published_documents (pg_trigger: none; content_versions has only content_versions_next_seq). An active owner or editor can therefore POST /rest/v1/content_versions with {collection:'scenes', doc_id:'gallery', data:{items:[{...,category:'سفر'}]}} and then POST /rest/v1/rpc/publish_version, and the document goes live. The build-time guard catches it: getScenes -> fetchPublishedOrNull (src/lib/content.ts:124-134) -> scenesSchema.parse throws ZodError, so the static build fails and the last good deployment stays live. A bad or malformed document fails the build. It is never skipped and never reaches a page, and an unresolved library id is skipped by sceneGallery. This is the settled D32 design, which admin-publish.ts:8-13 documents, and it matches every other collection. Separately, the name of the integration test at tests/integration/publish.test.ts:180, «...never goes live», overclaims: only the admin client path refuses.
findings.fix: No code change under D32. Rename the test at publish.test.ts:180 to say the admin publish refuses it. If the owner wants a database-side guard, that is a new migration adding a check in content_go_live for collection='scenes' (each items[*].category among the five, caption not blank).

findings.issue: One rule has no test: a published gallery that fails scenesSchema must make getScenes reject, which fails the build. Given the finding above, this build-time parse is the only server-side enforcement of the category and caption rules. W3 also rewrote the guard's code path (fetchPublished split into fetchPublishedOrNull, content.ts:124-142). A regression that returned null on a parse failure would render /scenes silently empty, and no test would fail.
findings.fix: In the 'the scenes at render time (C05)' block, add: servePublished([{ data: { items: [{ ...scenes[0], category: 'سفر' }] } }]); await expect(getScenes()).rejects.toThrow(); and the same with caption: '  '.

A hidden scene stays in the published document, which anon can read through /rest/v1/published_documents (policy published_documents_read using true). media_is_published also makes a hidden library image's id and derivatives anon-readable. This mirrors the rooms' hideable lists, as the brief asked. But C05 names 'rights', and an owner may use «إخفاء» for a photo whose rights are pending.
